key_insight: Augmenting video MLLMs with per-frame learnable camera tokens plus a pose regression module grounds frames in a shared spatial coordinate frame, enabling view-consistent temporal and spatial reasoning with minimal extra supervision.
problem_solved: Current multimodal LLMs treat video frames as independent 2D snapshots and lack persistent scene geometry, which hurts cross-frame grounding, spatial reasoning, and view-consistent understanding.
method: Attach a learnable camera token to each video frame to encode viewpoint-specific information alongside visual features.
Train a lightweight pose regression head (supervised by camera extrinsics or relative transforms) to predict per-frame camera poses and align frames into a shared 3D coordinate frame.
Fuse the camera tokens and predicted poses into the multimodal LLM pipeline so the model can reason about objects/actions consistently across viewpoints and time.
impact: Provides an efficient, low-cost way to inject explicit spatial structure into video MLLMs, improving temporal grounding, spatial reasoning, and downstream performance (e.g., video QA, tracking) without requiring dense 3D sensors.
visual_elements: Architecture schematic: frames → per-frame camera tokens → pose regressor → multimodal LLM
